A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their complete main texts, appendices, figures, tables, and algorithms are readable and support reliable matching across revisions and renumbering.

before.justification: v3 reports original video-generation experiments, quantitative comparisons in Table 1 and Figure 4, spectral analyses, and qualitative ablations.

after.justification: v4 retains those original experiments and adds quantitative monotonicity results, out-of-range generation examples, and an expanded training ablation.

M1.justification: The proposed joint backbone-LoRA and conditional-adapter training, deepest-third adapter placement, and selective LoRA removal at inference remain unchanged. Algorithm 4 documents the existing pyramid sampler; the partial-LoRA configuration is an added ablation, not a revised proposed method.

E1.justification: Appendix F adds an extrapolation scenario using conditioning values c = ±1.5 outside the training range [-1,1] for all three controls. The training domains, camera-control tasks, VBench prompts, and motion-centric evaluation coverage are otherwise retained.

E2.justification: The temperature-training comparison expands from joint versus adapter-only training in v3 Figure 12 to include deepest-third-only backbone LoRA and an explicit unadapted Wan2.1 reference in v4 Figure 13. The external comparators remain unchanged; CamEdit is newly cited but not evaluated.

E3.justification: Appendix E adds post-hoc evaluation of existing five-point sweeps using effect-specific image proxies and Spearman correlations over 15 shutter, 17 aperture, and 14 temperature prompts. Additional experiments introduce out-of-range sweeps and matched one-shot versus 30-shot training comparisons. Existing FEP/SVP protocols and general training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v4 substantially broadens supplementary validation: Appendix E quantitatively tests control monotonicity, Appendix F tests extrapolation beyond training support, and Appendix G.2 expands the training ablation to investigate backbone-LoRA coverage and scene diversity. These address distinct questions beyond v3's retained drift, inference, and joint-versus-adapter-only analyses.

E5.justification: The fixed-seed FEP and different-seed backbone baseline descriptions are retained. No repeated-run counts, uncertainty intervals, error bars, or significance tests are added. Table 2's correlations and prompt-wise summaries function as control-response metrics rather than uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Table 1 and Figure 4 retain their numerical results. New Table 2 reports mean absolute correlations of 0.987, 0.912, and 1.000 for shutter, aperture, and temperature, respectively, with median 1.000 and 100% direction accuracy throughout. New qualitative findings cover plausible extrapolation, partial-LoRA color bias, and weaker one-shot conditioning, extending the existing results without replacing the main performance comparisons.

T1.justification: The drift-rate definition, spectral criteria, and mathematical procedures in Algorithms 1–3 are retained. Algorithm 4 expresses the previously described sampling procedure as pseudocode; no new theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract is unchanged, and the introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: simple synthetic data enables efficient physical control, joint adaptation separates conditioning from domain shift, and drift diagnostics explain backbone preservation.

C2.justification: Section 2 narrows unrestricted backbone applicability to architectural compatibility with standard DiT backbones, leaving cross-backbone validation for future work. Section 5.2 explicitly limits FEP's temporal-quality interpretation. New appendix discussion interprets extrapolation, partial-LoRA bias, and scene-diversity effects, while acknowledging unresolved extrapolation limits and data scaling.

D1.justification: v4 adds a code/model access statement and repository link, plus Algorithm 4 specifying the existing pyramid sampling process. Hardware, optimizer, adapter dimensions, and training budgets remain unchanged. Conversely, Table 1 drops v3's Qwen-VL identification for the VQA scorer, reducing that detail without establishing an evaluator change.

R1.justification: v4 adds CamEdit and refines the distinction between camera-aware image methods and video adaptation. It removes the Evaluation Agent reference and redirects VBench citations to the benchmark paper. Consolidating the duplicate Shuttleworth reference and updating publication metadata do not introduce different underlying works.

P1.justification: v4 improves grammar and transitions, replaces clean/dirty inference terminology with Decoupled/Full-LoRA, and removes Good/Bad checkpoint labels. It folds Section 7.3 into Section 7.2 and adds appendix headings and cross-references while preserving the overall narrative structure.

P2.justification: v4 adds Table 2 and the extrapolation Figure 11, expands v3 Figure 12 into the training-comparison Figure 13, and rearranges the spectral figure. Table 1 gains grouped headers and baseline-proximity highlighting, Figure 10 receives a corrected caption, and several labels are updated. Most existing visual content is retained.

improvement.justification: v4 provides direct quantitative support for control monotonicity where v3 relied on visual sweeps, adds useful extrapolation and training-coverage checks, and improves applicability qualifications and sampling documentation. These strengthen the paper without changing its main results. The gains remain limited because the new evidence uses small proxy-based or qualitative evaluations without uncertainty reporting; dropping the Qwen-VL scorer label also slightly reduces reproducibility detail.
